author: m. t. shepherd
title: Rep Ryan Zinke calls for state control over grizzly management and comments on border policy
text:
Rep. Ryan Zinke, U.S. Congressman representing Montana’s 1st district since 2023, posted a series of statements on social media between March 23 and March 24, 2026, addressing wildlife management and national security issues.
On March 23, Zinke highlighted Montana’s unique bear population and recent conservation milestones. He wrote, “Today is World Bear Day. Montana is one of the few places in the USA that is home to both grizzlies and black bears. Incredible progress has been made on grizzly recovery. Let’s celebrate the win. Delist the grizzly and return management to the states.”
Later that day, Zinke criticized Democratic immigration policies and expressed concern over national security agency changes: “Democrats let thousands of unvetted people into our country with their open-border policies. Now they have shut down the agency that protects us from those domestic threats. This is a recipe for disaster, completely created out of the politics of the radical left.”
On March 24, he congratulated Markwayne Mullin on his appointment as Secretary of Homeland Security: “Congratulations to our new @DHSgov Secretary @SenMullin! America depends on your success as you continue reversing the disastrous results of the open border policies of the Biden administration. Ready to work with you to defend the homeland.”
Zinke was born in Bozeman, Montana in 1961 and currently resides in Whitefish at age 61. He previously served in the Montana Senate from 2009 to 2013 before joining Congress after Steve Daines in 2023. Zinke holds degrees from both the University of Oregon (1984) and National University (1991).
